# Overview

`FTucker3` is an R package for a **basis-preserving Tucker decomposition of
three-way functional data**. Each cell indexed by three structural modes contains
a trajectory observed on a common functional domain. The package implements the
FTUCKALS-3 alternating orthogonal estimation algorithm, along with Fourier
basis expansion, coefficient-tensor construction, reconstruction, diagnostics,
and structural-rank cross-validation.

This vignette presents a **small, self-contained illustrative example**. It
requires no Internet connection, downloads, or external data. The full NASA
POWER case study and the extensive Monte Carlo experiments documented in the
research are not run when this vignette is built.

# Mathematical formulation

Let $x_{ijk}(t)$ be a functional observation, with $i=1,\ldots,I$,
$j=1,\ldots,J$, and $k=1,\ldots,K$. For a fixed basis of $N$ functions,

$$
x_{ijk}(t) \approx \sum_{n=1}^{N} c_{ijkn}\,\phi_n(t).
$$

The coefficients form a fourth-order tensor
$\mathcal{C}\in\mathbb{R}^{I\times J\times K\times N}$.
FTucker-3 approximates this tensor as

$$
\widehat{\mathcal{C}}
 = \mathcal{G}\times_1 A\times_2 B\times_3 D,
$$

where $A\in\mathbb{R}^{I\times P}$,
$B\in\mathbb{R}^{J\times Q}$,
$D\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times R}$ are structural loading matrices, and
$\mathcal{G}\in\mathbb{R}^{P\times Q\times R\times N}$ is the
coefficient-domain core. The **functional-basis mode of length $N$ is not
compressed**. In the implemented Fourier case, the fitted curves are recovered
by evaluating the retained basis functions with reconstructed coefficients.

FTUCKALS-3 updates the three structural loading matrices through successive
conditional singular value decompositions (SVDs). Multiple random starts can
be requested; the starting fit with the smallest reconstruction error is
retained. As with standard multilinear factor models, individual loading
matrices may be subject to sign and rotational indeterminacy.

# Main functions

| Function | Purpose |
|:--|:--|
| `fourier_basis_matrix()` | Evaluate the Fourier basis on a time grid |
| `build_coefficient_tensor()` | Expand trajectories into a coefficient tensor |
| `ftuckals3()` | Fit the coefficient-domain decomposition |
| `ftucker3()` | Fit the integrated functional model |
| `coefficients_to_functional_array()` | Reconstruct trajectories from coefficients |
| `rank_cv_ftucker()` | Select structural ranks by cell-wise cross-validation |
| `mode_spectrum()` and `core_energy_table()` | Summarize fitted structure |

`ftucker3()` accepts an array of dimensions `I x J x K x M`, an observation
time grid of length `M`, structural ranks `(P, Q, R)`, a Fourier basis
dimension `N`, and a functional period `L`. If variables have different scales,
they should be standardized appropriately **before** calling the interface.

# Reproducible example: a low-rank functional tensor

We construct a small tensor that lies exactly in the FTucker-3 model class.
Its rank and Fourier basis are known. The example is **synthetic and intended
only to demonstrate the software interface**.

```{r example-data}
library(FTucker3)
set.seed(2026)

I <- 5L; J <- 4L; K <- 3L
P <- 2L; Q <- 2L; R <- 1L
N <- 3L; M <- 12L

t_grid <- 0:(M - 1L)
Phi <- fourier_basis_matrix(t = t_grid, N = N, L = 12)

A0 <- qr.Q(qr(matrix(stats::rnorm(I * P), I, P)))[, seq_len(P), drop = FALSE]
B0 <- qr.Q(qr(matrix(stats::rnorm(J * Q), J, Q)))[, seq_len(Q), drop = FALSE]
D0 <- qr.Q(qr(matrix(stats::rnorm(K * R), K, R)))[, seq_len(R), drop = FALSE]
G0 <- array(stats::rnorm(P * Q * R * N), dim = c(P, Q, R, N))

# Reconstruct the fourth-order coefficient tensor, retaining the basis mode.
C_true <- array(0, dim = c(I, J, K, N))
for (k in seq_len(K)) {
  for (n in seq_len(N)) {
    C_true[, , k, n] <-
      (A0 %*% G0[, , 1L, n] %*% t(B0)) * D0[k, 1L]
  }
}

# Evaluate all functional trajectories at the observed time points.
X <- coefficients_to_functional_array(C_true, Phi)
dim(X)
```

We now estimate the structural loading spaces and reconstruct the functional
tensor. `center = FALSE` is appropriate for this specific known low-rank example,
which was generated without additive marginal effects. With actual data,
preprocessing and the centering choice require substantive consideration.

```{r model-fit}
fit <- ftucker3(
  X = X,
  t_grid = t_grid,
  ranks = c(P, Q, R),
  N = N,
  L = 12,
  center = FALSE,
  max_iter = 200,
  tol = 1e-10,
  n_random_starts = 0
)

dim(fit$core)
dim(fit$reconstructed)
```

# Reconstruction and interpretation

```{r fit-diagnostics}
relative_functional_error <- sqrt(
  sum((X - fit$reconstructed)^2) / sum(X^2)
)

summary_fit <- data.frame(
  RelativeFunctionalError = relative_functional_error,
  CoefficientR2 = fit$optimization$R2_coeff,
  Iterations = fit$optimization$iterations,
  Converged = fit$optimization$converged
)
print(summary_fit)
```

A near-zero reconstruction error in this example checks recovery under an
**exactly specified, noise-free** model. It is not evidence of the same
accuracy on arbitrary observed data, and it does not replace validation with
real data or under perturbations.

```{r trajectory-plot, fig.cap="Observed and reconstructed trajectory for one tensor cell."}
plot(t_grid, X[1, 1, 1, ], type = "l", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Time", ylab = "Functional response")
lines(t_grid, fit$reconstructed[1, 1, 1, ], lty = 2, lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("Original", "FTucker-3 reconstruction"),
       lty = c(1, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n")
```

The fitted object exposes `fit$loadings` (three structural modes), `fit$core`
(the coefficient-domain core), `fit$functional_core` (the core evaluated over
time), `fit$basis`, `fit$reconstructed_coefficients`,
`fit$reconstructed`, and `fit$optimization` (fit diagnostics). Reconstructed
values can also be obtained using `predict(fit)`.

# Rank selection and further validation

A separate function performs cell-wise structural-rank cross-validation on a
**coefficient tensor**, rather than on raw trajectories. The following example
shows its interface; it is not evaluated while building this vignette because
rank search may require substantially more computation.

```{r rank-cv, eval=FALSE}
coeff <- build_coefficient_tensor(X, t_grid, N = 3, L = 12)$C
cv <- rank_cv_ftucker(
  C_raw = coeff,
  P_candidates = 1:2,
  Q_candidates = 1:2,
  R_candidates = 1,
  Kfold = 3,
  max_iter = 50
)
cv$selected
```

The package development process has also included independent tests of
controlled reconstruction, convergence across different Gaussian noise
levels, and numerical equivalence checks against the original thesis code.
Those development checks are **separate from this tutorial**, and their
results should be retained in reproducible validation records rather than
represented as new experiments performed by the vignette.

# Scope and citation

The current package implements the reusable computational core. The original
research additionally includes NASA POWER data preparation, leakage-free
cross-validation, Monte Carlo stress tests, Tucker-4 comparisons, and
computational scalability experiments. These research workflows are not all
part of the initial exported package interface.

If the methodology is used in scientific work, cite the associated article:

Cascante-Yarlequé, R., Galindo-Villardón, P., Guevara-Viejó, F., and
Vicente-Galindo, P. (2026). *A New Tucker Model for Three-Way Functional
Data: FTucker-3*. **Mathematics**, 14, 3589.
<https://doi.org/10.3390/math14193589>

`FTucker3` is under development and is not yet published on CRAN.
